newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Biscuit war leaves crumbs for both parties.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Biscuit war leaves crumbs for both parties.

text.p: London's High Court ruled in favour of McVities, makers of chocolate-coated biscuits Penguin on Tuesday, saying that supermarket chain ASDA Group Plc's look-alike Puffin brand had to be taken off the shelves within 35 days.
But in a classic case of both sides claiming victory, ASDA highlighted that Justice Walker had ruled the company could continue to keep the Puffin name, albeit with minor changes to the packaging.
Justice Walker found that Puffin does not infringe the Penguin registered name marks but that the packaging as a whole constituted "passing off".
The court also awarded costs and damages to McVities parent United Biscuits (Holdings) Plc. Ian McLeod, ASDA's grocery director, told Reuters the company was considering an appeal.
"We can continue to use the name Puffin and if we have got to make one or two minor tweaks to the packaging then we will consider those," said McLeod.
"The judgement is a bit puzzling because it is not clear what we are do to the packaging to satisfy ourselves there is no risk of confusion," he said.

ASDA has sold more than 40 million Puffin biscuits since it was launched last September and it has not received one letter of complaint from customers saying they had bought Puffins in mistake for Penguins, said McLeod.
The court's decision has been eagerly awaited by brand owners, retailers, consumers and lawyers as a guide to how future so-called "copycat" cases might be decided.
At stake for the brand holder are the huge costs in advertising and marketing which help support the brand and are reflected in higher retail prices.

Food and drink giant Grand Metropolitan Plc served a writ on ASDA in December alleging that four of its cheaper supermarket own label brands -- Daniel Boone's, Deep South, ASDA Peach Schnapps and Windward -- could be mistaken for GrandMet's branded and more expensive equivalent.
The case is due to be heard in June.

ASDA, seen as an innovator in the British supermarket industry, meanwhile is out to break the resale price fixing on over-the-counter medicines, having already contributed to the demise of the Net Book Agreement, which set retail prices for books. Britain's retail price maintenance system for medicines is currently under review by competition watchdog the Office of Fair Trading.

ASDA is chaired by Archie Norman, a Conservative candidate in the forthcoming election, and has focused on lower prices for a basket of goods along with an emphasis on fresh produce and larger stores which also feature clothing under the George brand along with other goods.
The company light-heartedly brought along individuals dressed in Penguin and Puffin suits to await the court's result on Tuesday.
